questions.question_text:
A game pays $\$15$ with probability $0.06$, $\$5$ with probability $0.3$, and nothing otherwise.
Find the expected prize.

options.why: Paired each prize with the other prize's probability, using $15(0.3)+5(0.06)$.
Averaged the three possible prizes $\$15$, $\$5$ and $\$0$ without weighting them.
Added the two prizes and ignored the probabilities entirely.

questions.question_text:
It costs $\$5$ to play a game that pays $\$30$ with probability $0.12$ and nothing otherwise.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: The game favours the operator: the expected net gain is $-\$1.40$ per play.
The game favours the player: the expected net gain is $\$3.60$ per play.
options.why: Found the expected prize but never subtracted the $\$5$ cost of playing.

options.text: The game favours the operator: the expected net gain is $-\$2.00$ per play.
options.why: Subtracted the $\$5$ from the prize before weighting and again at the end, charging the cost twice.

options.text: The game is fair, because $\$30 \times 0.12$ is close to the $\$5$ cost.
options.why: Treated 'close to' as equal; a fair game needs an expected net gain of exactly $\$0$.

questions.solution_text:
$E(\text{prize})=30(0.12)+0(0.88)$
$=3.6$
$E(\text{net gain})=3.6-5$
$=-\$1.40$
The expected net gain is negative, so the game favours the operator.

questions.question_text:
A game pays $\$25$ with probability $0.04$, $\$10$ with probability $0.15$, and nothing otherwise.
What entry fee would make the game fair?

options.why: Averaged the two prizes instead of weighting them by their probabilities.
Added the two prizes and ignored the probabilities.
Used only the $\$25$ prize's contribution and left out the $\$10$ prize.

questions.solution_text:
$E(\text{prize})=25(0.04)+10(0.15)+0(0.81)$
$=1+1.5$
$=2.5$
A fair entry fee equals the expected prize, so the fee is $\$2.50$.

questions.question_text:
A lucky dip barrel holds $10$ tokens: $5$ green paying $\$1$, $3$ yellow paying $\$4$ and $2$ red paying $\$10$.
One token is drawn.
Find the expected payout.

options.why: Swapped the yellow and red probabilities, using $1(0.5)+4(0.2)+10(0.3)$.
Averaged the three payouts and ignored how many tokens of each colour there are.
Added the three payouts without weighting them.

questions.question_text:
An insurer charges a $\$60$ premium and keeps it whatever happens.
With probability $0.05$ it must pay a claim of $\$400$.
Find the insurer's expected profit per policy.

options.why: Used $-\$400$ as the claim outcome instead of $\$60-\$400=-\$340$, dropping the premium.
Ignored the expected claim and gave the premium alone.
Gave the expected claim $\$400 \times 0.05$ rather than the expected profit.

questions.question_text:
A club game has an expected net gain to the player of $-\$0.85$ per play.
How much should the club expect to gain from $600$ plays?

options.why: Misplaced the decimal point, multiplying by $6000$ rather than $600$.
Gave the per-play figure instead of the total over $600$ plays.
Subtracted $\$0.85$ from $600$ instead of multiplying.

questions.solution_text:
The club gains $\$0.85$ per play on average.
Expected gain $=600(0.85)$
$=\$510$

questions.question_text:
Game $P$ pays $\$9$ with probability $0.25$ and loses the player $\$3$ otherwise.
Game $Q$ pays $\$4$ with probability $0.6$ and loses the player $\$5$ otherwise.
Which game should a player choose?

options.text: $Q$, because $E(Q)=\$0.40$ while $E(P)=\$0$, so only $Q$ has a positive expected net gain.
$P$, because its $\$9$ prize is the largest amount on offer.
options.why: Compared the largest prize instead of the expected net gain.

options.text: $P$, because a fair game is safer than one that can lose the player $\$5$.
options.why: Compared the worst possible outcome rather than the expected net gain.

options.text: Either, because both games give the player a real chance of winning.
options.why: Judged the games by the chance of a win rather than by the expected net gain.

questions.solution_text:
$E(P)=9(0.25)-3(0.75)$
$=2.25-2.25$
$=\$0$
$E(Q)=4(0.6)-5(0.4)$
$=2.4-2$
$=\$0.40$
Game $Q$ has the greater expected net gain, so a player should choose $Q$.

questions.question_text:
A game costs $\$3$ to play and pays $\$12$ with probability $0.2$, otherwise nothing.
Find the standard deviation of the net gain.

options.why: Stopped at the variance and did not take the square root.
Took $\sqrt{E(X^{2})}$ without subtracting $\mu^{2}$ first.
Gave the size of the expected net gain instead of the standard deviation.
